text:
maria: quick heads-up — I ran a small compare of streaming vs non-streaming across us-west1 (A100) and eu-west1 (H100). Wanted fast feedback before I write the ops doc.

benchmark-bot: started run 1876543210 — configs: SSE/http2 keepalive, WS/persistent, batcher=dynamic(128ms), quant profiles: fp16 & q4_0, kernels: triton vs cutlass. artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/1876543210/ (csv + traces)

ashwin: TL;DR numbers?

maria: TL;DR below — p50/p95 and max_qps at target p95=200ms:
- us-west1 (A100, fp16): SSE p50=48ms p95=120ms max_qps≈220
- us-west1 (A100, fp16): WS p50=60ms p95=160ms max_qps≈560
- eu-west1 (H100, q4_0): SSE p50=40ms p95=95ms max_qps≈330
- eu-west1 (H100, q4_0): WS p50=55ms p95=130ms max_qps≈780

kelly: interesting — WS wins on throughput especially on H100+q4. SSE keeps the tail lower on A100+fp16.

ryan: did you isolate kernel choice?

maria: yes — for A100 the triton matmul path gave ~10-15% lower p95 on SSE workloads. For H100, cutlass+alpa kernels sustained higher throughput under WS because of better multi-stream concurrency.

ashwin: quantization impact?

maria: q4 reduced memory bandwidth + CPU->GPU overhead, which helped batch packing for WS. But q4 + SSE + prefix caching yields the lowest tail latency on H100. On A100, fp16 + triton still had slightly better tail.

kelly: any perf cliffs from connection churn or heartbeat?

maria: WS has more steady packing, but gets worse p50 on small single-request spikes due to larger batching windows. SSE single-request p50 is lower because we flush earlier. We measured with these batching windows: SSE=8ms flush, WS=20ms pack (we tuned these).

ashwin: can you share the exact command/config used?

maria: command snippet:
```
./bench --model rwinf-gptx --protocol websocket --region eu-west1 --gpu h100 --quant q4_0 --batch_window_ms 20 --kernel_hint cutlass
./bench --model rwinf-gptx --protocol sse --region us-west1 --gpu a100 --quant fp16 --batch_window_ms 8 --kernel_hint triton
```

benchmark-bot: perf summary attached (CSV): p50,p95,max_qps per run. See s3 link above and internal dash: https://internal/dash/bench/1876543210

kelly: ops suggestion: prefer WS-backed streaming routes in H100 regions for high-throughput customers. Keep SSE endpoints in A100 regions as low-latency fallback. Also add a routing policy to prefer q4 on H100.

ryan: add a 10% canary and monitor quality regressions (eval suite + production prompts) before full roll. Any issues with prefix caching for WS?

maria: prefix caching works but we need to validate eviction behavior under WS when many clients hold long KV caches. Follow-up item: simulate KV churn.

ashwin: also call out kernel autotune — we saw variance across model lengths. Might be worth running a kernel sweep during model bring-up.

maria: will file a short playbook and a canary plan. ops config draft below:
```
route: /v1/stream
protocol: websocket
batch_window_ms: 20
quant_profile: q4_0
kernel_hint: cutlass
canary_pct: 10
monitoring: [latency,p95,eval-regressions]
```

kelly: perfect. can you attach the latency vs qps charts in the doc? I'll sync w/ sales for capacity guidance.

maria: will post graphs tomorrow (p95 vs qps, regional splits, kernel comparison). thanks everyone :thumbsup:
